title: Audit core RPM spec file anatomy and macro usage
input: An engineer authors an RPM spec file with hardcoded paths: `/usr/bin/myapp`, `/etc/myapp.conf`, and calls `make; make install` manually in `%build` and `%install`. How should this spec be refactored to use standard RPM macros and directories?
evidence_requirements: Replacement of hardcoded paths with %{_bindir}, %{_sysconfdir}, and %{_datadir}
Adoption of standard build macros (%make_build, %make_install, %cmake_build, or %autosetup)
Proper population of %files section using %config(noreplace) and %license

title: Leverage automatic RPM dependency generation and eliminate redundant manual tags
input: An RPM spec file includes manual tags: `Requires: libc.so.6, libpthread.so.0, libm.so.6, libssl.so.3`. Is this recommended in RPM packaging, and how does RPM handle dynamic library dependencies?
evidence_requirements: Explanation that rpmbuild automatically invokes find-requires and find-provides on compiled ELF binaries
Identification that manual soname Requires are anti-patterns that risk version drift and architecture mismatches
Removal of redundant manual library requires, keeping only high-level package or capability requirements

title: Remediate scriptlet execution trap during package upgrade and uninstall
input: An RPM package includes `%preun systemctl stop myapp.service` without checking `$1`. What disaster happens when the user upgrades the package from version 1.0 to 1.1?
evidence_requirements: Explanation of RPM upgrade sequence: new package %pre, new %post, OLD package %preun, OLD package %postun
Identification that unchecked %preun stops or disables the newly upgraded service when old package is uninstalled
Fixing with $1 == 0 check (or using standard %systemd_preun macros or file triggers)

title: Design split RPM subpackages for shared library and development headers
input: A C++ library project produces both a shared library `libbar.so.1` and development headers `bar.h`. How should the RPM spec be structured to create a base library subpackage and a `-devel` subpackage with strict architecture-bound dependencies?
evidence_requirements: Splitting %files: runtime .so.1* in base package, development .so symlink and headers in -devel package

title: Analyze RPM version sorting rules and pre-release tilde syntax
input: An engineer wants to package an alpha pre-release `2.0.0-alpha1` followed by final release `2.0.0`. If they set `Version: 2.0.0alpha1`, will RPM consider `2.0.0` an upgrade or downgrade? How should pre-releases be formatted in RPM?
evidence_requirements: Explanation that in RPM, alphabetic characters sort after nothing (2.0.0alpha1 is considered NEWER than 2.0.0)
Use of the tilde character (~) which sorts BEFORE everything (2.0.0~alpha1 < 2.0.0)
Recommendation of Version: 2.0.0 with Release: 0.1.alpha1%{?dist} or Version: 2.0.0~alpha1

title: Sign RPM package artifacts and verify signatures
input: An automated pipeline builds an RPM package. How does the release engineer cryptographically sign the package with GPG using rpmsign, and how can clients verify the package integrity?
evidence_requirements: Execution of rpmsign --addsign or rpm --addsign with configured GPG key
Verification of package signatures using rpm -Kv or rpm --checksig
Importing distribution public GPG key into rpmdb via rpm --import
